items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And this is what Rod Cless learned so very well, and learned it from Johnny Dodds, although he also admired Jimmy Noone.

ctx.x: They could hear at the time what was going on. They could hear what he was doing, and hear that no one else was doing it at that time. And that he was playing real New Orleans style clarinet, which -- a clarinet doesn't play like Benny Goodman, which -- in part of this number he's playing melody, part he's playing harmony and part he's playing -- the clarinet has a definite third position, just like the -- it's almost like barbershop. There's a melody that's sung out, and there's the bass part and then there's…

And this is what Rod Cless learned so very well, and learned it from Johnny Dodds, although he also admired Jimmy Noone. But he learned it very well. And many people didn't appreciate it, but I did. And you know who was a great fan of his? Bob Thiele And he gave us a date because of Rod Cless. He was a big fan at that time, yeah.
With a trio, wasn't it? (With [Jimmy] Butts on bass?)
